title: Publishing a Site for Free
text: These questions check that you can organize a site's files, use relative paths, publish and debug a site, and decide what belongs online.

tasks.text: A page at club-site/index.html shows an image stored at club-site/images/beds.jpg. Which src is right?
A photo shows on your computer but not online. The page says src="garden.jpg" and the file is named Garden.JPG. Why?
choices: Web servers usually treat file names as case-sensitive, so garden.jpg and Garden.JPG are different files
The server needs a new version

tasks.text: In the Network panel, style.css appears in red with status 404. What does that mean?
choices: The CSS has a syntax error
The browser asked for the file and the server couldn't find it

tasks.text: Before publishing, you notice members.csv, with members' phone numbers, in the site's folder. No page links to it. Is it safe to publish the folder? Explain.
tasks.answer: No. Every file in the folder is published, and anyone who guesses or finds its address can download it, whether or not a page links to it. Remove it from the folder before publishing.

tasks.text: Why can't a published web page keep an API key secret, even if the key is only in script.js?
tasks.answer: The browser downloads script.js to every visitor, and anyone can read it in the developer tools (or by opening its address). Anything sent to the browser is public; secrets must stay on a server.

tasks.text: Write a function riskyFileNames(names) that returns an array of the file names that contain a capital letter or a space. (Hint: name !== name.toLowerCase() is true when a name has a capital letter, and name.split(" ").length > 1 is true when it has a space.) Then write testRiskyFileNames, which logs riskyFileNames(["index.html", "Garden.JPG", "plant spacing.html", "style.css"]). (Expected: Garden.JPG and plant spacing.html.)

Start a new chat with your updated learner profile. Ask how to add a second page to your published site, plant-spacing.html with the calculator from an earlier lesson, sharing the same style.css, with links between the two pages. (1) Paste the reply. (2) Check every href and src: are they relative, and do the names match your files exactly? (3) Publish the update and test both pages and both links on a phone. Report any problems and how you found them.
tasks.answer: Full credit: all paths checked as relative with exact names; the update published; tests on a second device reported, with any 404s found via the Network panel. Replies vary, so grade the reasoning.
